div.head: I Cn 22.4
div.ab: Ac hu mæg þonne æfre ænig mann hinc inweardlice to Gode gebiddan, butan he hæbbe inweardlice (soðe lufe ⁊) rihtne geleafan to Gode?
Ac hu mæg ðonne æfre ænig man hine inweardlice to Gode gebiddan, buton he on God hæbbe inwardlice rihtne geleafan?
Ac hu mæg þonne æfre ænig man hyne inweardlice to Gode gebiddan, buton he on Godd habbe inweardilice rihtne geleafan?
Sed quomodo potest aliquis deuotas ad Deum preces effundere, qui non habet intime rectam fidem in eo?
[22, 4] Sed quomodo potest aliquis intimo corde Deum rogare, nisi habeat rectam credulitatem?
Quomodo poterit quisquam intime pro se Deum orare, qui erga Deum rectam fidem non habet?
Ac hu mæg ðonne æfre ænig man hine inweardlice to Gode gebiddan, buton he on God hæbbe inwardlice rihtne geleafan?
Ac hu mæg þonne æfre ænig mann hine inweardlice to Gode gebiddan butan he hæbbe inweardlice soðe lufe and rihtne geleafan to Gode?
Aber wie kann nun jemand jemals innig zu Gott beten, wenn er nicht innig (wahre Liebe und G) rechten Glauben zu Gott hat?
But how can anyone ever pray inwardly to God unless he has inwardly (true love and, G) true faith in God?
But how then can any man ever pray from the depths of his heart to God, unless he have true belief in God in the depths of his heart?
But how then can anyone ever pray to God in his soul unless he has true love for and faith in God in his soul?
div.note: ‘soðe lufe ⁊’ only in G. Liebermann compares Wulfstan p. 21.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 303, October 2026 (MS Cons)
